actions.action: Calculate all six totals from stated usage
actions.mechanism: A shared usage scenario exposes required add-ons instead of treating base prices as complete costs.
actions.implementation: Add labeled storage, editors, guests, and export inputs. Recalculate six itemized totals, including required charges and explicitly selected extras.
actions.check: For fixed usage fixtures, verify each total against an independently calculated bill; verify keyboard operation and screen-reader update announcements.
actions.risk: Unspecified usage must remain visibly unspecified, not silently become zero.

actions.action: Separate required charges from elective extras
actions.mechanism: Explicit charge categories prevent a needed add-on from appearing discretionary merely because it is sold separately.
actions.implementation: Show Included, Required for your usage, and Optional sections per plan. Keep optional extras unchecked; explain each requirement's trigger.
actions.check: Ask participants to identify charges they can remove without losing their stated capabilities; compare answers with structured charge rules.
actions.risk: An optional extra can become required when usage changes.

actions.action: Keep capability limits in one accessible matrix
actions.mechanism: Consistent rows expose differences and unavailable capabilities that scattered plan cards make difficult to compare.
actions.implementation: Use a semantic table covering all six plans and five capability categories. Write Included, Requires add-on, or Unavailable, with limits.
actions.check: Navigate every plan and capability with a screen reader; confirm unavailable features remain explicit at narrow widths and without color.
actions.risk: Dense tables need persistent labels and a usable narrow-screen layout.

actions.action: Explain what changes between two plans
actions.mechanism: A pairwise difference summary distinguishes similar offers through usage-specific costs, limits, and required extras.
actions.implementation: Let visitors select two plans for a supplemental textual comparison. Show total difference, charge differences, and capability tradeoffs; retain all six plans.
actions.check: Compare two equal-base-price fixtures with different required add-ons; verify the summary explains their differing totals without omitting unavailable capabilities.
actions.risk: A difference-only summary must not replace the complete comparison.

actions.action: Show the next cost-changing usage threshold
actions.mechanism: Boundary explanations reveal when a small usage increase triggers another seat, storage block, or export charge.
actions.implementation: Derive the next applicable threshold from charge rules and offer a labeled usage adjustment with before-and-after totals for every plan.
actions.check: Test usage immediately below, at, and above each threshold; verify charges and unavailable states match the rules.
actions.risk: Complex dependencies may require explaining several simultaneous changes.

actions.mechanism: A validated dependency model prevents missing mandatory charges and impossible capability combinations from producing misleading totals.
actions.implementation: Encode applicability conditions, quantities, dependencies, billing periods, and charge categories. Reject missing references and contradictory rules; mark invalid quotes unavailable.
actions.check: Inject a missing required add-on, circular dependency, and incompatible capability into fixtures; each must block a valid-looking quote.
actions.risk: Valid structure alone cannot establish that business rules are correct.

actions.action: Carry the comparison quote through checkout
actions.mechanism: A persistent itemized quote prevents selection and checkout from silently using different usage or charge assumptions.
actions.implementation: Pass usage, selected extras, and pricing-rule version to checkout. Revalidate server-side; show any changed total and explanation before confirmation.
actions.check: Run each plan through checkout using fixed scenarios; assert identical line items or an explicit change requiring renewed confirmation.
actions.risk: Expired pricing requires a visible refresh, not silent substitution.

actions.action: Test comprehension with deceptively similar plans
actions.mechanism: Scenario-based questions measure understanding of total cost and necessity rather than preference or perceived visual clarity.
actions.implementation: Use two similar-base-price plans with different required add-ons. Specify usage; ask participants for totals, removable extras, and unavailable capabilities before revealing answers.
actions.check: Score against predetermined answers, including screen-reader sessions. Record errors by charge category and revise misunderstood labels before repeating.
actions.risk: Leading prompts or repeated scenarios can inflate apparent comprehension.
